title: Police cleared of wrongdoing in fatal shootings
subtitle: The Special Investigations Unit has cleared Toronto police of wrongdoing in connection with two fatal shootings.
article: The Special Investigations Unit has cleared Toronto police of wrongdoing in connection with two fatal shootings.
In both cases, officers made "reasonable" decisions to fire their weapons based on evidence collected on the scene and witness testimony, SIU director James Cornish said in a statement.

The first incident took place last Halloween at Riverdale Park. According to the SIU, two officers drew their guns and surprised 18-year-old Alwy Al Nadhir and another suspect as they were robbing two men. The suspects were told to lie on the ground, but Al Nadhir tried to run. When an officer blocked his way the teen tried to fight him off.
"(Al Nadhir) grabbed the gun and then the struggle became one for control of the officer's gun," Cornish said. "(The officer) feared that he was going to lose control of it completely."

In the second shooting, 28-year-old Byron Debassige was gunned down in Oriole Park, after stealing lemons from a local grocery store at knifepoint, on Feb. 16. When officers tracked Debassige - a diagnosed schizophrenic - to the park, he pulled out his 3-inch blade and "advanced" toward them, said the SIU. Despite repeated commands, Debassige refused to drop the knife. In addition the ground was icy and sloped downwards.
Debassige was shot five times, said SIU spokesperson John Yoannou. The SIU is a civilian agency that probes cases of serious injury or death involving police.

"This whole ordeal has been very hard for me and my family," said Debassige's mother, Jennifene. She doesn't believe the SIU's version. "I'm not looking for blood money or anything, I just want answers."
One of the main concerns for Debassige and the Aboriginal Legal Services of Toronto is that police may have escalated the situation, prompting the mentally ill Debassige to get defensive.
"We really need to examine what could have been done," said Kimberly Murray, the group's executive director. They will be pushing for an inquest.
